title: Hierarchical retrieval: find a section before selecting its evidence
summary: Route through document structure while keeping answer citations on the smallest passage that actually proves the claim.
body:
Route through document structure while keeping answer citations on the smallest passage that actually proves the claim.

Index two useful levels

Hierarchical retrieval searches a document tree before choosing answer-bearing passages. A maintenance manual's chapter heading may say 'hydraulic pressure', while the relevant sentence appears in a child paragraph about pump P-47. Store a parent summary and child passages with stable IDs, revision and access label. The parent helps locate the right region; the child proves the claim. A heading alone is not evidence for a numeric limit. Chunk identity should preserve the original section path rather than replacing it with a generated synopsis.

Route with reversible decisions

A top-level search can choose candidate manuals, then section headings, then paragraphs. Keep more than one plausible branch when the query is ambiguous, and record each routing decision in the trace. If the first branch fails an evidence test, a bounded sibling search can recover a missed section. Do not let a model invent a chapter name or crawl indefinitely. Corrective retrieval needs a named failure and a fixed search budget, not an open-ended promise to look harder.

Apply permissions at both levels

A parent section might be visible while a child appendix is restricted. Filtering only the parent can expose child text; filtering only the child can reveal restricted section names through the navigation path. Bind tenant, role and revision to every node. If a parent is revoked, descendant eligibility must be recomputed or removed. An index generation should publish its tree and its passage store together, so a parent does not point to a child from an older revision. Document lifecycle rules still govern tree traversal.

Avoid parent dominance

Long section summaries can match many queries and crowd out precise passages. Allocate a small number of candidate parents, then a separate child window per parent; finally merge child passages with diversity controls. The result should carry its route and its actual supporting span. If the answer requires two sections, preserve both branches instead of concatenating one chapter's unrelated paragraphs. Context packing should count evidence coverage, not just total tokens.

Judge routing and support separately

Evaluation should report whether the right document was found, whether the right section survived routing, whether the supporting child reached the candidate window, and whether the answer cited it. Include misleading headings, appendices, renamed chapters, cross-section questions and restricted child nodes. A router may have high document recall but poor child recall. Preserve first-loss traces to locate that gap before changing the model or the prompt.

Worked contract

from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PassageNode:
    passage_id: str
    parent_id: str
    tenant: str
    revision: str
    text: str

def children_for_section(nodes: list[PassageNode], section_id: str,
                         tenant: str, revision: str, term: str) -> list[str]:
    return [node.passage_id for node in nodes
            if node.parent_id == section_id and node.tenant == tenant
            and node.revision == revision and term.casefold() in node.text.casefold()]

manual = [PassageNode("pump-47-limit", "hydraulics-r3", "plant-a", "r3",
                      "Pump P-47 relief limit is 83 kPa."),
          PassageNode("pump-47-old", "hydraulics-r2", "plant-a", "r2",
                      "Pump P-47 relief limit is 71 kPa."),
          PassageNode("private-limit", "hydraulics-r3", "plant-b", "r3",
                      "Pump P-47 relief limit is 99 kPa.")]
assert children_for_section(manual, "hydraulics-r3", "plant-a", "r3", "83 kPa") == [
    "pump-47-limit"]
assert children_for_section(manual, "hydraulics-r3", "plant-a", "r3", "99 kPa") == []

Performance and operating cost

This transparent child scan is O(N) time for N nodes and O(K) space for K matches. A production index keyed by parent, tenant and revision reduces the eligible scan, but tree traversal adds parent-search and child-search latency. Keep branch count and depth bounded; broad hierarchies can cost more than one flat retrieval call without improving support.

Common Mistakes

  • Citing a section summary that does not contain the claimed number.
  • Pruning every branch except the first plausible heading.
  • Applying access control to a parent but not its children.
  • Publishing a parent tree and child passages from different document revisions.

Validation drill

Index 23 manuals with three levels each. Judge 37 queries, including misleading headings and restricted appendices; report document, section and child-passage recall separately.

title: Late-interaction retrieval: score token matches without one-vector blur
summary: Compare multi-vector passage ranking with single-vector search while accounting for storage, candidate pruning and token-level false matches.
body:
Compare multi-vector passage ranking with single-vector search while accounting for storage, candidate pruning and token-level false matches.

Keep token evidence visible

A single vector compresses a whole passage into one representation. Late-interaction ranking keeps multiple token vectors for the query and passage, then combines their best token-level matches. This can preserve a rare part number alongside broad topic words. It is a ranking signal, not a proof that a passage answers the question: matching 'P-47', 'pressure' and 'limit' in separate sentences could still miss the requested limit. Claim support must inspect the actual text after ranking.

Separate candidate generation from scoring

Scoring every passage token against every query token is expensive. First build a candidate set with lexical or approximate vector search, apply tenant and revision filters, then run token-level scoring on a bounded window. If the correct passage never enters that window, late interaction cannot rescue it. Filtered candidate recall and reranker window size should be measured before debating score formulas.

Explain the aggregation

One simple late-interaction score takes each query token's best similarity to any passage token and sums those maxima. It rewards coverage of query terms while allowing different passage tokens to satisfy them. Normalize or calibrate for query length when comparing across questions; within one query, ranking scores can be compared directly. Stop words, duplicated tokens and template boilerplate can distort results. A document containing twenty copies of a part label should not gain twenty independent votes from one query term.

Budget memory and CPU

Multi-vector passages consume more index space than a single vector per passage. Token pruning, low-precision storage and candidate caps reduce cost, but each can reduce recall. Measure bytes per passage, index build time, p95 query latency and judged passage recall together. Keep encoder version and tokenization version on the index; a query encoded with a different vocabulary or model revision can change rankings without any corpus update. Embedding migrations need paired tests.

Test the hard queries

Include near-identical part numbers, terms scattered across unrelated sections, long passages, short passages and one genuinely absent answer. Report candidate recall, rank after late interaction, and final support separately. A high ranking score for a passage with all query words but no answer is an expected failure mode to catch, not a reason to weaken the citation check.

Worked contract

from math import sqrt

def cosine(left: tuple[float, ...], right: tuple[float, ...]) -> float:
    numerator = sum(a * b for a, b in zip(left, right, strict=True))
    left_norm = sqrt(sum(value * value for value in left))
    right_norm = sqrt(sum(value * value for value in right))
    if not left_norm or not right_norm:
        raise ValueError("zero-length token vector")
    return numerator / (left_norm * right_norm)

def token_coverage(query_tokens: list[tuple[float, ...]],
                   passage_tokens: list[tuple[float, ...]]) -> float:
    if not query_tokens or not passage_tokens:
        raise ValueError("empty token sequence")
    return sum(max(cosine(query, passage) for passage in passage_tokens)
               for query in query_tokens)

pressure_query = [(1.0, 0.0), (0.0, 1.0)]
complete_passage = [(1.0, 0.0), (0.0, 1.0)]
partial_passage = [(1.0, 0.0), (1.0, 0.0)]
assert token_coverage(pressure_query, complete_passage) == 2.0
assert token_coverage(pressure_query, partial_passage) == 1.0

Performance and operating cost

For Q query tokens, P passage tokens and D vector dimensions, direct scoring costs O(QPD) time and O(1) extra space beyond the vectors. For C candidates, multiply that work by C. Index storage grows with passage token count rather than passage count alone, so use a candidate stage and measure the cost of any compression or token pruning.

Common Mistakes

  • Running token-level scoring over the entire corpus without a candidate bound.
  • Treating token coverage as proof that the passage states the requested fact.
  • Mixing encoder or tokenizer revisions between query and index.
  • Ignoring storage growth when comparing against a single-vector baseline.

Validation drill

Judge 49 part-number questions with close distractors. Compare a single-vector baseline and a bounded token-level reranker on candidate recall, supported top-one answers, index bytes and p95 latency.

  • Embedding migrations: keep query and document vectors in one space
  • Claim-level citations: verify each answer against its passage

title: Temporal retrieval: answer as-of questions from valid evidence
summary: Distinguish when a fact was true from when it was indexed, and resolve overlapping revisions before producing a dated answer.
body:
Distinguish when a fact was true from when it was indexed, and resolve overlapping revisions before producing a dated answer.

Store two clocks

Temporal retrieval answers questions about a specified point in time. A policy may be valid from 1 March to 30 June yet ingested on 4 March. Valid time describes when the policy applies; system time describes when the search system learned or changed it. Conflating the two makes historical answers wrong after a late upload or backdated correction. Record both intervals and the source revision. Index freshness explains availability, while valid time determines which fact belongs in the answer.

Parse the user's time boundary

An as-of question needs a date, time zone and boundary convention. 'On 30 June' may mean any instant that day; an interval ending at midnight on 30 June may already be invalid then. Choose half-open intervals consistently: start inclusive, end exclusive. If the user gives only a month, do not quietly pick its last day for a rule that changed mid-month. Ask for a date or return the change range. Query routing should preserve the time constraint across every retrieval leg.

Filter before ranking

Restrict candidates to the requested valid-time interval and authorized corpus before semantic ranking. A newer policy is often lexically similar and may rank above the old one even when the user asks about last year. An answer must cite the applicable revision and the effective interval. For a comparison across dates, retrieve each date separately and keep the two evidence sets distinct. A revision's publication timestamp is not a substitute for its effective timestamp.

Resolve overlap explicitly

Two active records may cover the same instant because of a correction, overlapping jurisdiction or bad source data. Prefer a documented supersession rule only if the source provides one. Otherwise report the conflict with both citations and abstain from a single definitive value. A deletion may remove public availability without erasing the historical audit record; retrieval policy decides whether that archived evidence remains eligible. Access control applies even to historical answers.

Judge temporal slices

Build cases just before and after effective boundaries, retroactive corrections, delayed ingestion, unknown end dates, conflicting overlaps and no eligible history. Measure valid-revision recall and answer support separately from plain passage recall. A search that finds the right policy family but the wrong revision should fail the dated slice. Keep the corpus generation in the judgment so a changing source does not invalidate the comparison.

Worked contract

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PolicyRevision:
    revision: str
    tenant: str
    valid_from: date
    valid_until: date | None
    refund_days: int

def applicable_policy(revisions: list[PolicyRevision], tenant: str,
                      as_of: date) -> PolicyRevision | None:
    matches = [policy for policy in revisions if policy.tenant == tenant
               and policy.valid_from <= as_of
               and (policy.valid_until is None or as_of < policy.valid_until)]
    if len(matches) > 1:
        raise ValueError("overlapping eligible policy revisions")
    return matches[0] if matches else None

policies = [PolicyRevision("r3", "north", date(2026, 3, 1), date(2026, 7, 1), 47),
            PolicyRevision("r4", "north", date(2026, 7, 1), None, 29),
            PolicyRevision("private", "south", date(2026, 3, 1), None, 83)]
assert applicable_policy(policies, "north", date(2026, 6, 30)).refund_days == 47
assert applicable_policy(policies, "north", date(2026, 7, 1)).refund_days == 29
assert applicable_policy(policies, "north", date(2026, 2, 28)) is None

Performance and operating cost

The example scans R revisions in O(R) time and stores O(M) matches, where M is the number valid at the requested instant. A database interval index and tenant key can reduce candidate reads. Store valid-time and ingestion-time metadata separately; two extra timestamps are cheap compared with an unsupported historical answer.

Common Mistakes

  • Using ingestion time as the policy's effective date.
  • Treating an interval end as inclusive in one service and exclusive in another.
  • Returning the newest revision for every historical question.
  • Silently choosing one of two overlapping eligible revisions.

Validation drill

Create 61 dated questions around four policy transitions, including six backdated corrections and five overlaps. Require explicit ambiguity when the source cannot determine the applicable revision.

  • Retrieval query routing: preserve exact constraints before search
  • Retrieval evaluation labels: build a trustworthy judged set
  • Retrieval corpus contracts: identity, permissions and document lifecycle

title: Near-duplicate retrieval: collapse copies without hiding independent evidence
summary: Deduplicate copied passages by lineage and revision while preserving genuinely independent sources for corroboration.
body:
Deduplicate copied passages by lineage and revision while preserving genuinely independent sources for corroboration.

Separate copies from corroboration

A retrieval result can contain a policy paragraph copied into twelve team notes. Twelve hits are not twelve independent confirmations. Store document lineage, source owner, passage hash and revision so the system can group copies. Exact hashes catch byte-identical text; normalized hashes catch whitespace and formatting changes; semantic similarity can suggest near duplicates for review. A separate independent bulletin stating the same limit may be valuable corroboration and should not disappear merely because its wording is similar. Provenance decides which case applies.

Collapse at the right boundary

Group near duplicates after access filtering. A user who can see the public manual but not a private support note must not see the private note's title or existence in the collapsed result. Within an eligible group, choose an authoritative active revision and retain a list of permitted copies for audit. Do not pick a superseded revision only because it has a higher lexical score. Revision rules take precedence over ranking.

Protect the candidate window

Repeated template text can consume most of top-k, leaving no room for another document needed to answer the question. Collapse copies before context selection and reserve slots for distinct source lineages. Track both raw hit count and independent-lineage count in traces; a result of 20 hits from one copied memo is effectively one source. Evidence diversity should be measured at lineage level rather than URL count.

Choose a conservative similarity rule

A shared heading and two similar sentences do not prove two passages are duplicates. Numeric values, negations, dates and identifiers can differ while the rest of the text matches. Treat changes in those fields as blockers to automatic collapse. For uncertain pairs, keep both or flag them for review. False merging removes possible contradictions; false separation mostly wastes context. This asymmetry argues for conservative thresholds and explicit field checks.

Test both errors

Create copied passages, lightly reformatted copies, stale revisions and independently authored confirmations. Measure duplicate-group purity and answer-bearing passage recall after collapse. Include two near-identical policies whose refund windows differ and a copied note with a missing negation. The system should retain both contradictory policies for resolution, not merge them into a false consensus. Judged sets need lineage labels to make this visible.

Worked contract

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EvidenceCopy:
    passage_id: str
    tenant: str
    lineage: str
    revision: int
    text: str

def normalize_copy(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text.casefold()).strip()

def collapse_copies(passages: list[EvidenceCopy], tenant: str) -> list[EvidenceCopy]:
    chosen: dict[tuple[str, str], EvidenceCopy] = {}
    for passage in passages:
        if passage.tenant != tenant:
            continue
        key = (passage.lineage, normalize_copy(passage.text))
        if key not in chosen or passage.revision > chosen[key].revision:
            chosen[key] = passage
    return list(chosen.values())

copies = [EvidenceCopy("manual-r2", "north", "manual-47", 2, "Limit: 47 days"),
          EvidenceCopy("manual-r3", "north", "manual-47", 3, "Limit:  47 days"),
          EvidenceCopy("notice-r1", "north", "notice-83", 1, "Limit: 47 days"),
          EvidenceCopy("private-r4", "south", "manual-47", 4, "Limit: 47 days")]
assert {hit.passage_id for hit in collapse_copies(copies, "north")} == {
    "manual-r3", "notice-r1"}

Performance and operating cost

The hash-based baseline scans N passages in O(NL) time for average passage length L and stores O(U) groups for U unique lineage-text pairs. Semantic near-duplicate detection adds candidate-pair and review cost; avoid an O(N squared) all-pairs scan on a large corpus by blocking on lineage, source type or approximate fingerprints first.

Common Mistakes

  • Counting copied team notes as independent evidence.
  • Grouping before access checks and exposing restricted source metadata.
  • Merging passages that differ in a number, negation or effective date.
  • Keeping the highest-ranked stale copy instead of the active revision.

Validation drill

Make 79 passages across 12 lineages with exact copies, formatting changes, copied notes and three contradictory revisions. Verify that collapse preserves all independent answer-bearing sources and no restricted metadata leaks.

  • Document extraction: preserve passage provenance through OCR and parsing

  • Retrieval evaluation labels: build a trustworthy judged set

title: Chunking documents: preserve section identity and answer boundaries
summary: A chunk is a retrievable unit with text, document revision and structural context; its boundaries affect both recall and evidence quality.
body:
A chunk is a retrievable unit with text, document revision and structural context; its boundaries affect both recall and evidence quality.

Split on meaning first

A policy heading and its exception should remain connected. Blind fixed-character windows may separate the rule from a qualifying sentence and cause a plausible but wrong answer. Prefer section or paragraph boundaries, then enforce a size limit. Carry heading path, document ID, revision and exact offsets. Document identity] remains attached to every chunk.

Budget overlap deliberately

Small chunks improve pinpoint retrieval but can lose context. Large chunks carry context but consume more prompt budget and may rank by unrelated words. Overlap helps at boundaries but creates near duplicates. Count distinct parent documents in the final context so four overlapping chunks do not crowd out another necessary policy.

Preserve reproducibility

Version parser, normalization, chunking parameters and embedding model together. If extraction from a PDF changes line order, a stable document revision can still produce different chunks. Store a content hash and offset or section identifier for each passage. An answer audit should resolve exactly the passage the model saw, not today’s edited page.

Test difficult structure

Create a table-like policy with a footnote, a long section and two near-identical headings. Check that the exception stays retrievable with the rule. Verify each chunk respects its input limit and can be mapped back to an exact document revision. Retrieval evaluation] will show whether the chosen boundaries help real questions.

Implementation

import hashlib
import json

def make_chunk_id(document_id, revision, section_path, text):
    identity = json.dumps([document_id, revision, section_path, text], ensure_ascii=False)
    return hashlib.sha256(identity.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:24]

chunk_record = {"chunk_id": make_chunk_id(document_id, revision, section_path, passage_text),
                "document_id": document_id, "revision": revision,
                "section": section_path, "text": passage_text}

Performance and operating cost

Parsing and splitting C characters is at least O(C); embedding every chunk adds model cost proportional to chunk count and length. Overlap raises both index size and query-context duplication.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not separate an exception from the rule it qualifies.
  • Do not lose document revision and offsets when storing chunks.
  • Do not let overlapping chunks monopolize the context.

title: Reranking: spend model budget on a bounded candidate window
summary: Rerank a diverse, permitted candidate set and measure whether the added cost moves answer-bearing passages into view.
body:
Rerank a diverse, permitted candidate set and measure whether the added cost moves answer-bearing passages into view.

Find before sorting

A reranker can reorder candidates; it cannot recover an answer omitted by first-stage search. Freeze a judged set and measure candidate recall at the exact window passed to the reranker. Include identifiers, paraphrases, negative questions and long documents. If recall is weak, repair routing before paying for a bigger ranker. Hybrid retrieval can supply a stronger starting window.

Budget the input

Set a maximum candidate count, passage length and total scoring budget. A 47-passage window at 1,400 tokens each can cost more than the final answer. Truncate at sentence or section boundaries while retaining title and source identity. Test long queries and the largest eligible tenant. On timeout, fall back to first-stage order with a degraded-mode signal; do not disguise a timeout as no evidence.

Keep eligibility outside the model

Filter access, active revision and deletion state before scoring. A reranker should never see forbidden material, even if final selection would discard it. A high relevance score says nothing about truth, freshness or permission. Winning passages still need claim support checks.

Measure rank movement

Track first relevant rank, context-cutoff recall and answer support with and without reranking. Report by query family; a ranker may improve paraphrases while pushing exact IDs down. Retain candidate IDs, truncation details and model revision so regressions can be reproduced.

Worked contract

def bounded_rerank_window(candidates: list[dict], tenant_id: str,
                          limit: int = 12) -> list[dict]:
    if limit < 1:
        raise ValueError("candidate limit must be positive")
    selected, seen = [], set()
    for passage in candidates:
        if passage["tenant_id"] != tenant_id or passage["state"] != "active":
            continue
        identity = (passage["document_id"], passage["revision_id"], passage["span_id"])
        if identity not in seen:
            selected.append(passage)
            seen.add(identity)
        if len(selected) == limit:
            break
    return selected

candidate = {"tenant_id": "west", "state": "active", "document_id": "policy",
             "revision_id": "r8", "span_id": "p4"}
assert bounded_rerank_window([candidate, candidate, {**candidate, "tenant_id": "east"}],
                             "west", 2) == [candidate]

Performance and operating cost

Selecting K eligible passages from N candidates takes O(N) time and O(K) space. Pairwise reranking costs roughly one model evaluation per candidate, so compute grows with K and passage length. Cap both, measure p95, and separate first-stage recall from reranker gain.

Common Mistakes

  • Increasing the reranker window when the answer is absent from all first-stage hits.
  • Scoring a forbidden passage before access filtering.
  • Truncating away the sentence that carries the answer.
  • Calling a timeout fallback a successful rerank.

Validation drill

Use 91 judged questions. Compare first-stage and reranked first relevant rank at windows of 8, 16 and 32; record p95 latency and exact-ID regressions before choosing a window.

title: Index freshness: publish complete revisions and remove stale chunks
summary: Index updates need a versioned build, deletion handling and an atomic reader switch so answers never mix policy generations.
body:
Index updates need a versioned build, deletion handling and an atomic reader switch so answers never mix policy generations.

Build a candidate generation

When the support handbook changes, parse and index the new revision under a candidate generation. Keep the current generation serving while the candidate is incomplete. Validate document counts, active revisions, permissions and representative retrieval questions, then switch the reader pointer. Backfill publication] uses the same complete-before-visible idea.

Propagate deletion

A revoked policy can remain in an embedding index, lexical index or answer cache. Track document-to-chunk lineage so removal reaches every derived store. If a deletion cannot be completed promptly, deny access to the document ID at query time while reindexing catches up. Do not rely on an old vector disappearing merely because its source file was removed.

Choose freshness guarantees

Record ingestion lag, last successful index generation and maximum acceptable age. An urgent policy correction may require a synchronous block on old content; a routine edit may tolerate a short lag. Communicate when the answer feature is stale or unavailable rather than silently serving a superseded rule. No-answer behavior] can be safer during a gap.

Drill a partial failure

Fail one document during candidate indexing. The current generation should remain visible, the candidate should not publish, and an operator should see the rejected document and reason. Then revoke a permission and confirm query-time filtering blocks the old chunk before the next full rebuild.

Implementation

def publish_index(candidate, current_pointer, required_documents):
    if (set(candidate["document_ids"]) != set(required_documents)
            or len(candidate["document_ids"]) != len(set(candidate["document_ids"]))):
        raise ValueError("index generation is incomplete")
    if candidate["failed_chunks"] or not candidate["permission_checks_passed"]:
        raise ValueError("index generation failed checks")
    previous_generation = current_pointer.read()
    if not current_pointer.compare_and_swap(previous_generation, candidate["generation_id"]):
        raise RuntimeError("index pointer changed during publish")
    return previous_generation

Performance and operating cost

A full rebuild reads O(C) corpus content and creates O(K) chunks, embeddings and index entries. A pointer switch is cheap; storing two generations temporarily increases storage and build cost.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not expose a partial candidate index.
  • Do not forget answer caches when deleting content.
  • Do not wait for full reindexing to revoke access.

title: Context packing: retain independent evidence under a token cap
summary: Select passages by answer coverage, document diversity and provenance instead of filling the prompt with near-duplicates.
body:
Select passages by answer coverage, document diversity and provenance instead of filling the prompt with near-duplicates.

Reserve the evidence budget

Allocate tokens for instructions, question, response and citations before retrieved text. Each passage needs title, revision, section and citation identity. A long high-ranked section can crowd out a short exception that changes the answer. Pack by paragraphs or table rows, not a cut through a condition. Chunk boundaries determine what can be selected intact.

Prevent one revision from monopolizing context

Near-duplicate chunks often rank together. Limit repeated passages from one revision unless the question needs several clauses. Prefer a second independent source when it adds a missing fact, but do not force diversity at the cost of the sole answer-bearing span. Deduplicate the same passage identity across lexical and vector legs; copied text in separate revisions retains separate provenance.

Preserve contradictions

When permitted sources disagree, packing must not hide the newer statement just because it ranked lower. Include effective dates and revision labels so the answer can explain the conflict or abstain. Test exceptions, date boundaries and footnotes. Packet quality is whether it contains every fact needed, not its average similarity score.

Inspect the packet actually sent

Store candidate IDs, included IDs, exclusions and token counts. Compare generated claims with this exact packet, not the entire index. If support is absent, a fluent answer still fails. Claim checks decide whether to cite, revise or abstain.

Worked contract

def pack_passages(candidates: list[dict], token_budget: int,
                  per_revision_limit: int = 2) -> list[dict]:
    if token_budget < 1 or per_revision_limit < 1:
        raise ValueError("positive limits required")
    selected, spent, per_revision = [], 0, {}
    for passage in candidates:
        revision = (passage["document_id"], passage["revision_id"])
        if per_revision.get(revision, 0) >= per_revision_limit:
            continue
        if spent + passage["tokens"] > token_budget:
            continue
        selected.append(passage)
        spent += passage["tokens"]
        per_revision[revision] = per_revision.get(revision, 0) + 1
    return selected

ranked = [{"document_id": "policy", "revision_id": "r8", "tokens": 33},
          {"document_id": "policy", "revision_id": "r8", "tokens": 41},
          {"document_id": "faq", "revision_id": "r3", "tokens": 29}]
packet = pack_passages(ranked, 67, 1)
assert len(packet) == 2 and sum(p["tokens"] for p in packet) == 62

Performance and operating cost

This bounded pass costs O(K) time and O(D) counters for K candidates and D revisions. Tokenization and model context cost dominate. Greedy packing can miss a better combination; add measured coverage-aware selection only if judged queries expose that ceiling.

Common Mistakes

  • Spending the whole context window on passages and leaving no response budget.
  • Suppressing a newer contradiction because its score is lower.
  • Confusing duplicate text with duplicate source identity.
  • Citing a passage that was retrieved but not included in the final packet.

Validation drill

For 37 questions, label required facts and revisions. Pack under a 540-token evidence budget and measure how often all facts survive, especially exceptions and conflicts.
